architecture.topology: Lobby Fabric process owns admission/directory/durable shared-state authority; A and B Fabric workers own disjoint whole gameplay dimensions. MTMC coordinates route/transfer hooks. Static ownership, private per-dimension storage; no shared world/SQLite file or live rsync.
architecture.initialization: Same full registries/recipes/mod manifest. Only assigned gameplay levels tick/load/save. Explicitly refactor vanilla Overworld bootstrap and mod server.overworld() dependencies; real startup gate must prove no duplicate writable gameplay dimension. Do not use a writable unowned world as fallback.
architecture.transport: Dedicated mTLS gRPC peer port, generated protobuf, shaded Netty, node identity/cluster allowlist. WebSockets simpler and familiar but need custom typed protocol/flow control; raw TCP adds framing. Choice is maintainability, not measured performance.
architecture.protocol: Version/node/boot/cluster IDs, op+transfer UUIDs, object UUID, owner epoch, expected revision, deadline and digest. Durable phase-specific ACKs, idempotent inbox and durable outbox. Bounded requests/bytes, backpressure, heartbeat, deadlines, exponential reconnect, ledger reconciliation; reject schema/registry mismatch. Proposed heartbeat1s/unavailable5s/RPC5s/prepare15s/reconnect0.25-5s; freeze values and queue limits before run.
architecture.threading: I/O and persistence off tick threads; bounded commands applied on actual world/region owner queue. Pending/frozen actions rather than join/get waiting for RPC; within-process mod communication stays local.
architecture.durability: Single local SQLite WAL writer, synchronous FULL; transactional ownership CAS, snapshots/digests/revisions, transfer ledger, shared transactions, receipts/outboxes. Real mod business logic uses explicit command backends. Mirrors never authorize spending. No automatic authority failover; authority outage pauses critical operations.
architecture.transfer: REQUEST -> QUIESCED -> SNAPSHOT_DURABLE -> DEST_PREPARED -> OWNER_COMMITTED -> CLIENT_REDIRECTED -> ACTIVATED -> SOURCE_CLEANED. Gate source mutations/death/pickup/menu operations and drain shared transactions. Capture complete player+attachments+mod state preserving cursor/crafting exactly once. Destination prepares inert state/arrival. Durable owner CAS after source quiescence and destination preparation; only committed destination can activate.
architecture.admission: Validate native 26.2 client transfer with actual Fabric/EndInv clients. One-use short-lived destination/session ticket bound to authenticated UUID+epoch over peer channel; ticket is not a substitute for identity authentication. Lobby reconnect reads committed owner; backend login requires admission. Offline lab identity fixtures clearly labeled. If native transfer/mod handshake fails, report gate failure and seek approval for proxy adaptation.
architecture.recovery: Precommit durable abort can restore source; postcommit recover only destination. Replays return original committed result. Stale playerdata cannot overwrite ledger/reactivate old epoch. Timeout alone never grants competing ownership: durable quiesce or proven process fencing required. Authority restart reconciles workers before admitting sessions; unknown outcomes remain unavailable.
architecture.entities: Capture full passenger/entity tree, retain UUIDs, source durable tombstones and load filters, destination dedup before activation. Include leashes/pearls/mob/item portals; unsupported serialized types explicitly fail/block.
architecture.endinv: Real mod/client with async cluster backend. One authoritative actor/revision per inventory UUID, central ACL/selection, one station scheduler using cluster presence. Include SourceInventory add/take, crafting, autopick, loot, stations, admin and sync; preserve legacy IDs. Replace cluster-mode Overworld SavedData authority, retain local backend for baseline.
architecture.coupled_operations: Durable operation IDs/escrow for EndInv<->player/menu/item entity/reward/economy. Reserve input/record intent, commit authoritative deltas, idempotently materialize output on owner queue; journal recovery reconciles partial local application. Drain before transfer capture. Test partial-apply crashes; snapshot+ACK alone insufficient. Vanilla world saves outside supported operations remain disclosed limits, not blanket no-loss claims.
architecture.emma_smp: Route all teleports/admin/ghost/respawn paths and cross-node tpa; commit back/cooldowns on success. Single ownership of economy/jobs/limits/roles/lifesteal/directory/homes/warps/claims/guild/market/events and schedules; local block effects stay dimension-local with event IDs. Permissions globally consistent.
architecture.sync_API_risk: CommonEconomyBridge and SourceInventory return synchronous results today. Adapt known consumers to async reservations/commit. Never return success before durable commit, use stale caches for spending or block tick on RPC. Enumerate external consumers; unavailable integrations explicit BLOCKED, no silent coverage reduction.
architecture.other_mods: Mob-targeting refreshes after travel; bridge/cache keys use logical cluster+dimension identity and state resync. Configure real LuckPerms coherently; pin Lithium/ServerCore. Optional maps and other consumers audited before claiming coverage. Moonrise excluded as declared incompatible.

acceptance.correctness: Zero unexplained conserved-state deltas, zero simultaneous active owners/stale writes, all durably acknowledged critical operations survive tested process crashes. Explain intentional consumption/death/decay with conservation equations.
acceptance.recovery: Recovered or explicit unavailable state within60s after dependencies reachable; no consistency trade for timeout reassignment; no watchdog/deadlock/unbounded queues.
acceptance.proposed_capacity: 30min steady plateau: TPS>=19.5 each60s window; worker/lobby p95 MSPT<=50ms,p99<=100ms; healthy transfer p95<=2s,p99<=5s. Thresholds proposed for approval; all samples/worst windows reported.
acceptance.metrics: Raw tick p95/p99, sustained TPS, dimension/main thread/phase, CPU/process/host/quota/throttle, RAM/heap/GC, disk, network bytes/RTT/retries/queues, transfer stage and end-to-end latency, generator CPU/RAM/action completion/backlog. Existing MTMC aggregates need raw tick/main-thread instrumentation.
acceptance.interpretation: 100 remains estimate,300 goal; active vs ghosts separate; regionalization incremental gain separate from MTMC. Single-host coordination not multi-PC performance. Added hardware vs same aggregate CPU budget separate; hot dimension limit explicit.

harness.freeze: Pin all commits/JAR/dependency hashes/config/seed/script/threshold/workload manifests across hosts; collect clock skew. Preserve unchanged original baseline.
harness.result_schema: Each test JSON PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT RUN; exit code0/1/2/3 respectively; expected+observed, reason, versions/commits/hashes, per-node limits, configuration/seed/workload/metrics/evidence paths. Runner emits all scheduled records; skipped or blocked never PASS.
harness.execution: Complete independent scenarios safely after failures; stop only suite blocker or data risk, preserve evidence, mark remainder explicitly. No patch/threshold/config change or causal diagnosis midway.
harness.review: After complete run group behavioral/consistency/harness/resource/environment failures. Unchanged targeted diagnostic reruns with purpose recorded. Approval before fixes; targeted tests plus full regression after approved fixes.

risks: Overworld/bootstrap assumptions and sync APIs make this broader than adding a transport.
Native transfer/custom payload handshake/cache identity unverified; possible proxy/client adaptation gate.
World/player/EndInv/economy partial application requires explicit escrow/recovery.
Single shared authority/EndInv actor may bottleneck; no HA prototype.
A hot whole dimension still has one owner budget; regionalization only its measured incremental benefit.
4core single-host tests cannot establish300-player multi-PC performance.
Historical314 joins/passive ghosts/poor TPS not proof of300 active playable players.
